resolutions.recommendedParking: Parcheggio Rifugio Auronzo (P1), beside Rifugio Auronzo. Use the mapped parking-area centroid as the navigation pin, not the tollgate or the refuge building.
accessFacts: The official Auronzo source identifies the large parking area beside Rifugio Auronzo as the road-access trailhead.
Online reservation is mandatory for car access; the published 2026 car tariff is €40.
The mapped centroid is supported by the current OSM-derived parking record but is not a guarantee of a particular bay or entrance.
Parking can be approved separately; the candidate's stored route relation remains invalid and blocks ORMA verification.

resolutions.recommendedParking: Bai de Dones chairlift forecourt is both the start and finish. The selected pin is the parking/trailhead coordinate published by Cortina Marketing's verified route record.

parkingOptions.label: Bai de Dones parking – 5 Torri chairlift

accessFacts: The verified Cortina route record names Bai de Dones parking as the start and end and publishes the coordinate.
Its route description uses the chairlift for the ascent and returns to Bai de Dones on trail 425.
The route record reports 4.2 km and 2 hours when using the chairlift; a fully walked version has different distance, time and ascent.
The summer road to Rifugio 5 Torri is closed from 6 June to 20 September 2026, so it must not be presented as the routine driving trailhead.

resolutions.recommendedParking: Rifugio Aquileia is a confirmed alternative access anchor at 46.43629, 12.10065, but it is not approved as a substitute start for the stored full Giro del Pelmo loop.
accessFacts: Rifugio Aquileia publishes its own coordinate and confirms it is open for summer 2026.
Rifugio Città di Fiume currently states that paths 467 and 472 from the Staulanza side are interrupted and directs visitors via Rifugio Aquileia.
CAI San Vito's current trail-status page warns against the 472 line along the west scree beneath Pelmo because of rockfall risk.
A 9 August 2026 regional news report describes three recent rockfalls and continuing municipal monitoring; this increases rather than clears uncertainty.
No authoritative approved detour for the complete stored loop was found in attempt 2.
